summary: Switches the batched live-input GraphQL query from the deprecated nullable 32-bit review databaseId to fullDatabaseId and parses it strictly as a positive decimal safe integer, so a null legacy id can no longer fail an entire repository chunk and force per-record REST fallback. New hermetic wire tests cover 60 records across two chunks plus exact, malformed and unsafe id handling, and a repair-loop regression drives 60 live records through the real GitHubApiClient over a fake HTTP port, asserting one successful batch, no per-record fallback read and preserved unchanged-input skips. No throughput threshold was raised.

evidence: src/github/client-live-inputs.ts lines 104-107 now query reviews(last: 1) { nodes { fullDatabaseId } } and lines 240-256 validate it as a positive decimal within the safe integer range, replacing the nullable 32-bit databaseId that failed a whole repository chunk.
tests/github/client-live-inputs-review_test.ts keeps 60 records in two chunks with review id 2^31+17, accepts MAX_SAFE_INTEGER exactly, and rejects unsafe, malformed and non-string ids.

tests/repair/loop-input-gate_test.ts lines 646-742 drive 60 live records through the real GitHubApiClient on a fake HTTP port and assert batchUnavailable 0, batchReads 1, no readIssue/readRef fallback calls, 60 unchanged-input skips, and re-stepping when the review id changes.
src/host/throughput-watchdog-thresholds.ts is untouched, so no threshold was raised to make the metric pass.
